findings.location: Paragraph with speed metaphor (source.html paragraph: "It is as though you are in a vehicle traveling 90 mph...")
findings.source_quote: It is as though you are in a vehicle traveling 90 mph, and you push the accelerator a little harder, and nothing happens.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the added parenthetical conversion or make it verbatim to the source. Either delete "(ongeveer 145 km/u)" or move it outside the quoted metaphor as an editorial note, preserving the original phrasing without numeric conversion.
findings.translation_quote: Het is alsof je in een voertuig rijdt met 90 mph (ongeveer 145 km/u) en je drukt het gaspedaal iets verder in en er gebeurt niets.

findings.source_quote: I Samuel 30 tells the story of David returning to Ziklag.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same book numbering style as the source for clarity. Change "1 Samuel 30" back to the source style "I Samuel 30" if the publication prefers Roman numerals; if Arabic numerals are the house style, no change is needed. This is an editorial consistency suggestion rather than a theological correction.
findings.translation_quote: 1 Samuel 30 vertelt het verhaal van David die terugkeert naar Ziklag.
